CHAPTER III 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH THE 
COMMITTEE DOES NOT ACCEPT THE REASONS GIVEN BY THE DEPARTMENT 
AND REITERATES ITS RECOMMENDATIONS 
LACK OF AWARENESS AND LEGAL EDUCATION 
Recommendation/Observation  
3.1  Therefore, empowering individuals through education and creating awareness about their 
rights and the role of legal aid is essential to bridge this informational gap. Accordingly, the 
Committee is of the view that Government may take an extensive mass media campaign to 
educate the eligible population about the legal aid avenues available for them to get justice. (Para 
10)  
Action Taken:  
 
I. It is submitted that National Legal Services Authority (NALSA) is bridging the 
information gap among the eligible population with its ongoing awareness programmes. 
During the year 2023, 3,44,580 physical legal awareness programmes were organized 
which benefitted 3,21,50,1 78 persons. The increase in number of persons availing legal 
services reflects the impact of existing awareness programmes: 
A. The number of persons availing free legal services including legal representation, 
assistance, and advice increased by 36% in the year 2023 (14.9 lakh) in comparison to 
the year 2022 (10.9 lakh). 
B. The number of persons availing legal services at pre-arrest stage, arrest and remand 
stage increased by 30% from 1. 7 lakh in the year 2022 to 2.2 lakh in the year 2023. 
II. NALSA regularly conduc ts legal aid camp -based awareness campaigns across the 
country and has developed a NALSA 'theme song' for media -based awareness on the role 
of NALSA. However, NALSA has not yet ventured into mass -media campaigns at the 
national level. For mass -media campai gns, there will be need of specially qualified 
human resource having experience in media and communications for designing, 
coordinating, and analyzing mass -media campaigns. In order to bridge the information 
gap, it is proposed that NALSA will adopt following two pronged approach: 
A. Strengthening the existing awareness programmes/ campaigns: 
Conducting Pan-India beneficiary category wise targeted legal awareness campaigns, 
as per a fixed calendar/schedule of campaigns. The campaigns would include: 
i. Legal Literacy and Awareness camps: Tailored programs will be developed with 
focused attention on specific subject matters and rights & obligations, and 
processes under related laws. 
ii. Community outreach: Public events/meetings, street plays, etc. by students and 
PLVs. 
iii. On-spot legal services: Legal counselling & assistance camps by engaging 
lawyers (Panel Lawyers and Legal Aid Defence Counsels {LADCs}) with 

 
17 
subject-matter expertise; 
iv. Information Dissemination: Outreach -kits containing flyers, posters, etc. in local 
languages regarding the role of Legal Services Institutions (LSIs) and legal 
services schemes, programmes, etc. will be distributed. 
v. Mobile clinics for remote areas: Utilize vehicle based legal aid clinics for remote 
areas and small communities, including nomadic and semi nomadic communities. 
vi. Student PLV involvement: Encourage University based legal aid clinics for 
conducting follow-up legal awareness and outreach camps in areas in the vicinity 
of their institutions. 
vii. Reporting and Feedback: District Legal Services Authorities (DLSAs) will 
prepare categorized data of the campaigns which will be analyzed at the state 
level by the State Legal Services Authorities (SLSAs) and at the national level by 
NALSA for identifying improvement areas and sharing of good p ractices among 
SLSAs. 
B. Building capacity for "extensive mass media campaign to educate the eligible 
population about the legal aid avenue ": 
i. NALSA will take assistance of a special government agency in designing, 
executing, and analyzing mass media campaign s, from the earmarked funds for 
this purpose. 
ii. Local campaigns will focus on digital and physical dissemination of NALSA's 
Information, Education & Communication (IEC) material such as posters and 
flyers on legal services schemes, eligibility under Section 12 of the LSA Act 
1987, platforms/means for accessing legal services, etc. 
iii. These mass -media and physical campaigns will be synchronized with the 
scheduled targeted campaigns as proposed in part 'A' of the proposed action. 
iv. To enhance the dissemination of th e 'theme song', NALSA will coordinate & 
collaborate with mass -media platforms such as All India Radio, Doordarshan, 
Rajya Sabha TV, Lok Sabha TV, etc. for playing NALSA's theme song. 
v. SLSAs and DLSAs will ensure the widespread distribution of NALSA's theme 
song at public events, market areas, community fairs/carnivals, etc., in the local 
language. 
Further Recommendation/Observation 
 
3.2 Despite NALSA's commendable efforts, legal awareness remains limited, 
particularly in rural and marginalized communities. Awareness is crucial for the success of 
legal aid mechanisms. Therefore, the Committee recommends that NALSA collaborate 
with educational institutions and NGOs to integrate legal literacy into curricula, leverage 
mass media and digital platforms to  disseminate information widely  and regularly assess 
the impact of these initiatives through surveys and feedback mechanisms to ensure 
effectiveness. 
 
BUDGETARY CONSTRAINTS AND ALLOCATIONS 
Recommendation/Observation 

 
18 
3.3 It is an admitted fact that the prevalent social and economic disparity in the country is 
eroding the democratic objective of 'justice for all'. As majority of our population lacks legal 
awareness and necessary means to approach the courts, they are compelled to suffer in silence. 
Legal aid is an obligation of the State and rights of the Citizen, accordingly, it should be 
provided in the true spirit as envisaged in the Constitution. (Para 14) 
Action Taken: 
I. It is submitted that during April, 2023 to December, 2023, the Legal Services Authorities 
organized 3,55,850 legal awareness programs by engaging its 42,412 lawyers and 42,782 
PLVs, which benefitted 3,21,50,178 persons across the country. 
II. NALSA launched the revamped National Legal Aid Helpline 15100 on the Legal 
Services Day 2023 to enhance the reach of Legal Services Institutions and bridge the gap 
of access in remote areas and for persons under circumstances of restricted mobility. 
Between 09.11.2023 and 26.12.2023 (47 days), 84,235 persons were assisted though the 
helpline for their legal queries, requests, emergency services, legal assistance, etc. 
III. It is proposed that NALSA will increase the number of PLVs on the basis of a need-based 
assessment at the SLSA level.  
IV. It is further submitted that NALSA has informed that during the regular confer ences and 
meetings, majority of the SLSAs have expressed budgetary constraints as the prominent 
challenge in achieving the intended outcomes of legal services programmes. Section 16 
of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 mandates State governments to provide funds 
to the State Legal Services Authorities (SLSAs). It has been decided by NALSA to take 
up this issue with the SLSAs at the State / Regional conferences. 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
3.4   In this regard, the Committee observes that the majority of the Indian population are eligible 
for legal aid. However, as per 'India Justice Report, 2019' published by the Tata Trust, per capita 
free legal aid s pend in India is just 0.75 paisa  per annum (in 2017 -18), which is perhaps among 
the lowest in the wor ld. Though funding legal services authorities is also one of the 
responsibilities of States, there is a dire need to significantly enhance the expenditure on this 
front. Therefore, the Committee strongly recommends that Grant -in-aid to NALSA may be 
substantially increased in order to carry out the activities as planned by them. (Para 15) 
Action Taken: 
I. The majority of the population is 'eligible' for legal aid as per the wide eligibility criteria 
given under Section 12 of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987. Wide eligibility 
framework ensures that no one in need of free legal services is rendered ineligible to 
receive the services. It may be noted that 'eligibility' does not necessarily mean 'need' 
and therefore every eligible person for legal aid may not need free legal services. 
II. During the F.Y. 2022 -23, Rs. 190 crore were provided to NALSA as Grant -in-Aid for 
free legal aid activities which were increased to Rs. 200 crore during F.Y. 2023-24 during 
Budget Estimate stage. Further, the Government of India  has approved a new Central 
Sector Scheme namely Legal Aid Defense Counsel System (LADCS) Scheme for three 
years (F.Y. 2023-24 to F.Y. 2025 -26) with outlay of Rs. 998.43 crore (including Rs. 200 

 
19 
crore for F.Y. 2023 -24 for implementation and operationalizat ion of LADCS Scheme) 
with 100% Central share. Hence, total Rs. 400 crore were provided to NALSA during the 
F.Y. 2023-24.  
III. In absence of adequate funds from the State governments, SLSAs are dependent on 
NALSA grants only. To address this issue, it is propos ed that NALSA will take steps for 
deliberating this issue at appropriate platform for finding sustainable and decentralized 
funding solutions. 
IV. It is further proposed that NALSA will request a specialized government agency such as 
NITI Aayog to conduct a pa n-India survey for demand and supply of free legal services 
as well as to map the anticipated increase in demand. Such a study will be crucial in an 
objective determination on the required funds and human resources to meet the demand. 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation 
 
3.5 Budget limitations impede the scalability and effectiveness of legal aid programs, 
affecting infrastructure, staffing, and outreach activities. The Department of Justice's 
DISHA program, which reached 1.53 million individuals through legal awareness 
initiatives as of June 30, 2024, demonstrates the potential impact of well -funded programs. 
Therefore, the Committee advocates for a fixed percentage of state GDP to be allocated to 
legal aid, encouraging state contribut ions through matching central grants, and exploring 
partnerships with the private sector and CSR initiatives to supplement funding and ensure 
sustainable resource allocation. 
 
ROLE OF LAWYERS AND COMPENSATION 
Recommendation/Observation 
3.6 As regard s fee , it is being observed that panel lawyers are not being adequately 
compensated and their remuneration has remained stagnant for years together. This affects the 
quality of legal aid service provided to the clients. This also often leads to lawyers found 
harassing beneficiaries or demanding 'fees' from them. The Committee accordingly, recommends 
NALSA to compensate lawyers adequately, so that they are able to sustain themselves and 
remain motivated in their job. While ensuring this, a robust system of monitori ng the efficacy 
and accountability of legal aid services provided to the beneficiaries may also be put in place by 
NALSA. (Para 22) 
Action Taken: 
I. Regulation 14 of The National Legal Services Authority (Free and Competent Legal 
Services) Regulations, 2010 provides that the SLSAs and other LSIs "shall effect periodic 
revision of the honorarium to be paid to panel lawyers". 
II. The Central Authority of NALSA vide its meeting dated 17.09.2015 constituted a 
committee on this subject -matter. The Committee proposed th e following minimum fee 
structure: 
At High Court Level 
Drafting of substantive pleadings  Rs. 1500  

 
20 
Drafting of miscellaneous applications Rs. 500  
Appearance per effective hearing  Rs. 1000  
Appearance per non-effective hearing Rs. 750  
(maximum of Rs. 10,000 per case) 
Subordinate Courts at all levels including Tribunals 
Drafting of substantive pleadings  Rs. 1200  
Drafting of miscellaneous applications Rs. 400  
(maximum of Rs.800 for all applications) 
Appearance per effective hearing  Rs. 750 
Appearance per non-effective hearing Rs. 550  
(maximum of Rs. 7,500 per case) 
 
III. Under Legal Aid Defense Counsel Scheme (Modified) 2022, the LADCs are paid a 
competitive retainership fee or honorarium up to Rs. 1 Lakh per month to Chief LADCs, 
up to Rs. 75, 000 per month to Dy Chief LADCs, and upto Rs. 45,000 to Assistant 
LADCs. 
IV. With respect to the "robust system of monitoring the efficacy and accountability of legal 
aid services provided to the beneficiaries", it is submitted that the Monitoring and 
Mentoring Committees (MMCs) are set up at the district level under Rule 10 of the 
National Legal Services Authority (Free and Competent Legal Services) Regulations, 
2010 which undertake case-to-case monitoring of the  functioning of the LADCS, in line 
with the monitoring of the cases assigned to the Panel Lawyers. 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation 
 
3.7 Efforts to encourage pro -bono work and enhance lawyer compensation are 
progressing, yet the absence of structured in centives and formal recognition continues to 
deter widespread participation. Recognizing the vital role of effective legal representation, 
constitutional courts have emphasized the need to strengthen free legal aid services, 
particularly for prisoners. To address this, the Committee recommends establishment of a 
national registry for pro-bono lawyers, offering recognition and linking their contributions 
to career advancement opportunities, such as senior designations or judicial appointments. 
Additionally, annual reviews of compensation rates should be institutionalized to align with 
market standards, ensuring the recruitment and retention of committed legal professionals. 
 
UNDERUTILIZATION OF PARA-LEGAL VOLUNTEERS 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
3.8 To overcome these challenges and enhance the utilization of PLVs Committee feels that 
some immediate measures should be taken like providing regular and comprehensive training 
and capacity building of PLVs. They should also be provided with adequate resour ces and 
support to perform their duties effectively. PLVs should be paid or compensated adequately for 

 
21 
their work, so that they remain interested in their work. They should also receive recognition and 
appreciation from the legal system and the society. Th is would enhance their motivation and 
commitment to serve the people. Further, the legal services authorities and the Lok Adalats 
should conduct awareness campaigns and outreach programs to inform and educate the people 
about the role and functions of PLVs . In turn, the PLVs should also build trust and rapport with 
the people and address their concerns and grievances. (Para 26) 
Action Taken 
I. There are 42,782 PLVs, out of which 17,765 (41.5%) are female, 235 are transgender 
persons and 24,782 are male, who ha ve been given induction training. In addition to the 
induction training, 7,407 PLVs have been provided special training through various  
capacity building programmes during the last five F.Y. i.e. 2019-20 to 2023-24. 
II. As per the Scheme for Para -Legal Volunte ers (Revised), the PLVs' tenure may be 
extended for more than a year if the Chairperson, DLSA finds the PLV's performance 
satisfactory based on regular review. 
III. NALSA periodically organizes national level programmes for PLVs for recognizing and 
commending t heir performance. The State authorities also regularly organize similar 
programmes at the State level. 
IV. In reference to the issue of providing adequate resources to the PLVs, it may be noted 
that the expenses incurred by the PLVs in performance of their dut ies, including travel 
costs, are reimbursed as per the 'Scheme for Para Legal Volunteers (Revised).' 
V. In reference to the issue of payment and adequate compensation to the PLVs for their 
services, it may be noted that the SLSAs and DLSAs decide the honorar ium for the PLVs 
as per the revised Scheme (referred above). As per the Scheme, revised in the year 2013, 
the honorarium of the PLVs shall not be less than Rs. 250 per day. As of January, 2024, 
the honorarium for PLV in different SLSAs ranges between Rs. 250 to Rs. 1800 per day. 
VI. It is proposed that NALSA will ensure that intensive subject-specific trainings for PLVs 
are conducted at the district level based on their area of work and experience, in 
collaboration with the local organizations and government bodies. Further, SLSAs will be 
asked to ensure that the PLVs are empanelled under all categories as mentioned in the 
revised scheme. 
VII. It is further proposed that the agenda of revising the minimum fee structure for PLVs will 
be taken up in the next Central Au thority meeting of NALSA. In addition, all campaigns 
of NALSA will include awareness about the specific roles of PLVs. Pamphlets and 
posters displaying the details of the PLVs in the district/taluk a along with their subject -
specific roles will also be publicized at relevant public places. 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation 
 
3.9 Para-Legal Volunteers (PLVs) remain an underutilized resource despite their 
potential to connect marginalized communities with essential legal services. Their 
effectiveness can be significantly enhanced through expanded roles, targeted training, and 
meaningful recognition. To bridge existing gaps, the Committee recommends training 

 
22 
programs should incorporate digital literacy, mediation techniques, and specialized legal 
skills relevant to local needs. Performance-based incentives must be introduced to motiva te 
consistent excellence, while peer -review mechanisms can foster collaboration and identify 
best practices for replication. Recognizing top -performing PLVs through awards and 
public acknowledgment will further enhance their commitment and inspire broader 
participation, ultimately strengthening the grassroots reach of legal aid services. 
 
MANNING THE NALSA  
 
Recommendation/Observation  
3.10 The Committee notes that NALSA's activities have increased manifold since its inception 
and it is actively engaged in taking the legal aid movement in India to every nook and corner. 
However, its existing sanctioned staff strength of 34 only is too low considering its mandate and 
reach. Accordingly, the Committee recommends the Government to sanction additional 40 posts 
as requested by them. (Para 33) 
Action Taken 
I. It is submitted that NALSA is working on the proposals for creation of additional posts 
for NALSA and Department of Justice will act on it as per due process. 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation  
 
3.11 The Committ ee has repeatedly emphasized the urgency of this issue, but the 
Department's responses have been consistently vague and non -committal. NALSA has 
frequently highlighted this concern during its depositions, underscoring the critical 
need for adequate staffin g to fulfil its expanding mandate. The Committee strongly 
recommends that the Department of Justice provide a clear and actionable timeline 
for the creation and recruitment of the requisite officers and staff in NALSA. Such a 
commitment is essential to ens ure the effective functioning of NALSA and the 
fulfilment of its objective to provide accessible and efficient legal aid services across 
the country.

CHAPTER I 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN 
ACCEPTED BY THE DEPARTMENT 
Raising the stature of Notaries in India  
Recommendation/Observation 
1.1 Notaries do not receive any remuneration or pay from the government. The 
only source of their income is the fees they charge from their client. The fees to be 
payable to a notary for doing any notarial act are prescribed under Rule 10 of the 
Notaries Rules, 1956. The prescribed fee is meagre, and it was last updated in the 
year 2014. Thus, there is a need to appropriately raise the fees commensurate with 
inflation so that the notaries can have a decent standard of living. Accordingly, the 
Committee recommends that the government to increase the fee payable to notaries 
and make it inflation-linked. It should be revised at regular intervals, preferably every 
five year. (Para 3.3) 
Action Taken: 
1.2 The recommendation of the Committee has been, in principle, accepted and 
accordingly, Rule 10 of the Notaries Rules, 1956 is being suitably amended to 
rationalize and increase the fees to be charged by the Notaries for various purposes. 
 
Sanctioned Strength of Notaries  
Recommendation/Observation 
1.3 It is the considered view of the Committee that the criteria for deciding the 
sanctioned strength of notaries in a state is very vague and lacks objectivity at all. 
The sanctioned strength of notaries in a particular state should be determined on the 
basis of its population, volume of litigation, economic and commercial activities in 
that state, etc., and it should be reviewed regularly. (Para 3.9) 
Action Taken: 
1.4 The number of Notaries to be appointed by the Central Government in various 
States and UTs has been re-calibrated with reference to the State-wise data of 
population (Census: 2011); Gross State Domestic Product at Current Price for 2021-
22 (Source: RBI); State-wise GST collection for the month of November, 2023 and 
pending cases as on 22.12.2023 (Source: National Judicial Data Grid of Department 
of Justice). The geographical landscape and area of the States have also been taken 
into consideration. Based on these rational parameters, the strength of Notaries to be 
appointed by the Central Government in various States has been revised, vide the 

 
10 
 
Notaries (Amendment) Rules, 2024, notified on 24th February, 2024.  In view of this, 
the recommendation of the Committee stands accepted and implemented. 
 
Use of technology in appointment and notarial work  
Recommendation/Observation 
1.5 Presently, the Notary Portal of the Department of Legal Affairs 
(https://notary.legalaffairs.gov.in/) is used for submitting applications and declaring 
results only. With the advancement of technology, the Department needs to harness 
its full potential for making significant improvements in the appointment process. 
The Committee, therefore, recommends the government make this portal a one-stop 
place for advertising vacancies of notaries, making applications, submitting fees, 
publishing results, and downloading e-certificates of practice. The entire process of 
renewal of the certificate of practice should be made through this portal only. 
Further, the annual returns under rule 14 of the Notaries Rules, 1956, should also be 
filled online through this portal. (Para 3.15) 
Action Taken 
1.6 The Department has launched a new Notary Portal (https://notary.gov.in) on 
3.9.2024.  It provides an online interface between the notaries and the Government 
for various services like submission of applications for appointment as notaries, 
issuance and renewal of Certificates of Practice, change of practice area, submission 
of annual returns, etc.  With the launch of the Notary Portal, the Central Notaries will 
not be required to submit applications/ requests in physical mode.  They can submit 
applications online; monitor its progress; and download digitally signed Certificates 
of Practice from their digilocker accounts.   
  
1.7 The Notary Portal has different modules, to be rolled out in phases. In the first 
stage, module relating to issue of Certificate of Practice to the provisionally selected 
Notaries has been launched. Other modules relating to renewal of Certificate of 
Practice, submission of Annual Returns, change of area of practice, etc will be rolled 
out gradually in a phased manner. 
  
1.8 All features recommended by the Committee are being incorporated in the 
Notary Portal.  In view of this, the recommendation of the Committee may stand 
accepted and complied, when all modules of the notary portal (https://notary.gov.in) 
will go live. 
 

 
11 
 
Diversity in notaries' profession  
Recommendation/Observation 
1.9 On this issue, the Committee feels that notaries' profession should reflect the 
diversity of the State in which they are appointed. This will further enrich the notarial 
profession and the legal system. Accordingly, it is recommended that the government 
should appropriately give representation to SCs, STs, OBCs, Women, Physically 
Challenged, Minorities, etc., in the appointment of notaries. Further, at the 
application stage, the candidate should be asked to furnish their category so that the 
Department maintains category-wise data. Accordingly, the rules may be amended to 
that extent. (Para 3.19) 
 
Action Taken:  
 1.10 In order to ensure proper representation of SCs, STs, OBCs, Women and 
PwBD, the applicants of these categories are required to have lesser experience, 
compared to other applicants. Further, the new Notary Portal will capture category 
wise data. Form I of the Notaries Rules, 1956 has also been amended vide the 
Notaries (Amendment) Rules, 2024, notified on 24.2.2024, wherein provisions have 
been made to capture the data related to SC, ST, OBC, Women, PwBD, etc.  
 
 
 
Change of Notarial Year for furnishing the annual return 
Recommendation/Observation 
1.11 The demand for changing the Notarial Year from calendar year to financial 
year seems logical, and this will help the notaries to synchronize their returns with 
that of Income Tax returns. Accordingly, the Committee recommends changing the 
Notarial Year from Calendar to Financial Year. (Para 3.23) 
 
Action Taken: 
1.12 The recommendation of the Committee to change Notarial year from Calander 
to financial year has been accepted and necessary amendment in this regard is being 
made in the Notaries Rules, 1956.

THE REPLIES GIVEN BY THE DEPARTMENT 
 
Appointment of Notaries  
Recommendation/Observation 2.1  The Committee accordingly recommends doing away with interview-based 
appointment of notaries. Instead, the selection should be based on an objective type 
written examination along the lines of the All India Bar Examination (AIBE) 
conducted by the Bar Council of India (BCI). In fact, the Central Government may 
consider using the same examination i.e. AIBE, which is conducted twice a year by 
the BCI, for getting the panel of central notaries. (Para 3.6). Action Taken: 
2.2 The recommendation made by the Committee has been examined and the 
following alternatives are under active consideration of the Government for selection 
and appointment as Notaries: 
(i)         replacing the process of interview by written examination; or 
(ii)        introducing written examination for initial screening of the applicants and 
calling only such applicants who qualify the written examination for the interviews. 
 2.3 Since the appointment of Notaries as per existing provisions of the Notaries 
Rules, 1956 is already in progress, the above alternatives will, however, be made 
effective after completion of the current round of appointment process in the 
remaining States and UTs.   
 2.4 Accordingly, necessary amendment will be made in this regard in the Notaries 
Rules, 1956. 
 
Qualification for Appointment of Notaries  Recommendation/Observation 
2.5 On this, the Committee opines that the 10 years of practice as eligibility for the 
appointment is on the higher side, and it should be reduced to 5 years to attract young 
aspirant lawyers to this profession. At the same time, it should also be made 
mandatory for the applicant to have appeared in at least 100 cases. (Para 3.11) 

 
13 
 
 
Action Taken:  
 2.6 The recommendation of the Committee has been examined and it has been 
decided, in principle, to reduce the experience prescribed for appointment as a Notary 
to 7 years, relaxable to 5 years for SC/ ST/ OBC/ PwBD and Women applicants. 
 Accordingly, a suitable proposal to amend the Notaries Rules, 1956 is being moved. 
 2.7 As regards the recommendation regarding prescribing minimum number of 
appearances in Courts, it is mentioned that presently there is no such requirement of 
appearance in cases for being considered for appointment as a Notary.   It may be 
functionally and administratively very difficult to verify the claims of the applicants 
on this aspect.  Therefore, the present system may continue.  
 
Training of Notaries  
Recommendation/Observation 
2.8 Notaries should be equipped to handle electronic transactions, digital 
documents, and online notarization. For this training of notaries should be made. 
(Para 3.17) 
 
Action Taken: 
2.9 It is proposed to make the Notary Portal user friendly. Further, a detailed 
booklet for the help of the users will also be developed and made available on the 
Notary Online Portal. 
 
Designated areas for sitting of notaries  Recommendation/Observation 
2.10 The Committee recommends the government to ensure designated areas for the 
sitting of notaries in every Court complex from where they can do their notarial work 
in a dignified manner. (Para 3.21) 
 
Action Taken:  
 2.11 The recommendation of the Committee is outside the jurisdiction of this 
Department.  The recommendation of the Committee is being forwarded to the State 
Governments for taking appropriate action on the recommendation. 
 
 

 
14 
 
 
CHAPTER III 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS IN RESPECT OF 
WHICH THE COMMITTEE DOES NOT ACCEPT THE REASONS 
GIVEN BY THE DEPARTMENT AND REITERATES ITS 
RECOMMENDATIONS 
 
Renewal of certificate of practice  
Recommendation/Observation 
3.1 Almost all the stakeholders flagged the issue of delay in the renewal of 
certificate of practice. They all brought to the notice of the Committee that there are 
allegations of corruption and misuse of discretion in the renewal process. On the 
renewal process, the Committee think that it is being done only to know about the 
antecedents of the applicant and to ensure that the applicant is alive and nobody else 
is practicing in their place.  The Committee is, therefore, of the view that renewal of 
certificate of practice every five years should be done away with. After their 
appointment, notaries may be allowed to practice till a particular age prescribed by 
the government. As the government has the power to suspend or remove notaries on 
a complaint received against them, this will empower the government to tame the 
erring/defaulting notaries. In order to access the antecedent of the notaries and 
confirm they are alive, the Committee desires that a system like online self-
certification or otherwise may be suitably devised by the government. (Para 3.14) 
 
Action Taken: 
3.2 Several steps have been taken to ensure that Certificate of practice of the 
Notaries are renewed in a timely manner. More than 4900 Certificates of Practice 
(CoP) of Central Notaries have been renewed since January, 2023.  Further, the 
Government has launched a new Notary Portal, i.e. https://notary.gov.in, which will 
enable the Notaries to submit their applications for renewal online after the module 
relating to renewal of Certificates of Practice is made live. The Government is also 
working on replacing the physical CoP by digitally signed CoP, which will also be 
available on Digi-locker.  Incidentally, CoPs to the newly appointed notaries are 
digitally signed and are being issued online and are also available in the Digi-locker 
of the Notaries concerned.     

 
15 
 
3.3 Considering the above, the present system may continue.  However, the 
recommendations made by the Committee have been noted and based on the 
experiences gained after full operationalization of the online system, and after 
stakeholder consultation, further improvement in the system will be brought, so as to 
bring more transparency and efficiency.  After reviewing the functioning of the 
Notary Portal, the possibility of reforming the renewal process by amending the 
Notaries Act, 1952 will be explored.  
 
Further Observation and Recommendation: 
 
3.4 The Committee welcomes the steps taken by the Department to renewal of 
Certificates of Practice on time. However, the core concern regarding 
eliminating periodic renewal still remains unaddressed. The Committee's 
recommendation to allow notaries to practice until a prescribed age, subject to 
disciplinary oversight, aims to reduce discretion. The Government should 
consider this proposal after full portal implementation and if necessary consider 
a statutory amendment to introduce one time certification till the prescribed age 
with periodic self-declaration, ensuring both accountability and procedural 
simplification. 
 
Use of technology in appointment and notarial work   
Recommendation/Observation  
3.5 Additionally, the general public should be provided with a state-wise list of 
public notaries, updated on a real-time basis, for verifying the credentials of notaries.  
The public may also be allowed to raise grievances/complaints against notaries 
through this portal. In the long run, the services of this portal may be extended to the 
States and UTs so that the common public can access central and state notaries in one 
place. (Para 3.16) 
 
Action Taken: 
3.6 Once all modules in the Notary Portal become operational, the Register of 
Notaries, as provided in the Notaries Rules, 1956, will get updated on real time basis 
and will be in public domain on the Notary Portal.  To this extent, the 
recommendation made by the Committee will stand accepted and implemented after 
all the modules of the Notary Portal go live. However, as regards recommendation of 
the Committee regarding raising grievances against Notaries through online portal, it 

 
16 
 
is stated that Rule 13 of the Notaries Rules, 1956 prescribes an elaborate procedure 
for inquiry into the allegations of professional or other misconduct of a Notary.  It 
requires that every complaint shall contain the acts and omissions which, if proved, 
would render the person complained against unfit to be a Notary; and the oral or 
documentary evidence relied upon in support of the allegations made in the 
complaint are subjected to examination and corroboration.  The said Rule further 
prescribes that a copy of the complaint shall be sent to the Notary for a written 
statement in his defence verified in the same manner as a pleading in a civil court.  It 
further provides for inquiry in the matter by the Competent Authority.  Considering 
the complexities involved, implementation of the recommendation of the Committee 
does not appear feasible.  However, in order to expedite disposal of complaints 
against Notaries, the Central Government has designated an Officer of the 
Department of the level of Deputy Legal Adviser as Competent Authority solely for 
the purpose of Rule 13 of Notaries Rules, 1956. 
 
Further Observation and Recommendation: 
 
3.7 While the real-time public availability of the Register of Notaries is a 
welcome step, the non-acceptance of an online grievance mechanism limits 
public accessibility and transparency. Considering the increasing digitalization 
of public services, the Committee is of the opinion that a preliminary online 
grievance submission system may be introduced to streamline complaint intake, 
which can then proceed under the existing Rule 13 framework.  
  
 
 
Notarizing of documents  Recommendation/Observation 
3.8 The notarial work should be modernised and digitised, and the use of 
electronic signatures, stamps, and seals should be encouraged. The notarial records 
and certificates should be stored and maintained in a centralised online database, 
which can be accessed and verified by the concerned authorities and parties. The 
notaries should also adopt uniform formats and standards for their documents and 
certificates. (Para 3.26) 
3.9 The Committee accordingly, recommends the government to ensure that all 
public notaries maintain a digital register to keep records of documents notarised by 

 
17 
 
them. Digitalizing records will help avoid fraud, deceit, and tampering of records. 
The concept of digital signature should be introduced so that records are not 
antedated and to identify such notaries who indulge in fabrication or falsification of 
documents. (Para 3.27) 
 
Action Taken:  
 3.10 Implementation of this recommendation involves developing an appropriate 
software for the works performed by the Notaries. Such software will need to have an 
interface between the Notaries and the Public at large. There will also be a 
requirement of necessary infrastructure at the end of Notaries, in the absence of 
which the entire exercise will be futile. The burden on Notaries for procuring and 
maintaining digital infrastructure and their readiness to shift to digital mode also 
needs to be looked into in greater details. The implementation of this 
recommendation also involves the question of data security and privacy.  Cost of 
digital infrastructure also needs to be weighed in. Further, in order to maintain 
uniformity with the States/ UTs, the availability of digital infrastructure with these 
Governments needs to be looked into.   
3.11 While the Department is committed to bringing transparency and efficiency in 
the system, the implementation of recommendation required further deliberations 
with the stakeholders. 
 
Further Observation and Recommendation: 
 
3.12 The committee is of the opinion that the digitization of notarial records, 
introduction of digital signatures, and maintenance of a centralized database is 
crucial for ensuring transparency and preventing tampering. While 
infrastructure and cost concerns are valid, the lack of a definitive timeline or 
roadmap delays critical reform. The Department should initiate this process 
with willing notaries and pilot states, by providing necessary support and 
training.  
Training of Notaries Recommendation/Observation 
3.13 Thus the Committee is of the view that the notaries should be provided with 
regular training and guidance, and their performance and conduct should be 
monitored and evaluated by an appropriate government/ authority. Also, some ethical 
and professional standards should be laid out by such government/ authority to which 

 
18 
 
notaries should adhere to. Further, any complaints or grievances against the Notaries 
should be promptly addressed and resolved. (Para 3.29) 
 
Action Taken:  
 3.14 The Department has launched a new Notary Portal (https://notary.gov.in), 
which will work as a dedicated platform for all issues related to the Notaries.  As 
regards prescribing ethical and professional standards for the Notaries, it is stated that 
even after appointment as Notaries, they continue to be legal practitioners, and as 
such, are bound by the ethical and professional standards prescribed in the Advocates 
Act, 1961.  Other recommendations made by the Committee has been noted for 
further action. 
Further Observation and Recommendation: 
3.15 Launching of Notary Portal is a positive step, the absence of dedicated 
ethical and professional standards specifically tailored for notarial functions is 
absent. Notarial duties differ from general legal practice and require distinct 
accountability mechanisms. The government should frame specific codes of 
conduct and performance benchmarks for notaries, establish a monitoring 
framework to ensure timely grievance redressal through the portal, which will 
enhance transparency and public trust in notarial services.

CHAPTER I 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN 
ACCEPTED BY THE MINISTRY 
Recommendation/Observation 
1.1.  The Committee while extending its appreciation to the Election Commission of 
India for their diligent efforts in conducting free and fair elections in the country and 
recommends that citizens should have greater transparency when it comes to the 
Common Electoral Roll and the integration of Aadhaar with EPIC. However, it is 
important to note that linking Aadhaar with Voter ID is voluntary and not obligatory. 
(Para 1.48)   
 
Action Taken 
 
1.2 Comments of this Department: In this regard, it may be stated that the said 
recommendation pertains to the ECI and they have submitted the comments as 
under:-  
1.3 Comments received from the ECI: “The Commission vide its letter no. 
23/inst/2022-ES dated 04.07.2022 has issued instructions to the CEOs of all the states 
and UTs for starting a programme to collect the Aadhar Number of the existing 
electors. A new Form 6B has been devised for electors who have already been 
enrolled in the electoral roll for providing their Aadhar details voluntarily. Further, 
the process of linking of Aadhaar with voter id has not been started yet. Further, the 
Commission is also considering amendments and modifications to the relevant 
provisions related to linking of Aadhar with Voter ID and enrolment Forms in view 
of Hon'ble Supreme Court's direction in the matter. It has been emphasised that the 
linking of Aadhaar with voter ID should be voluntary and not obligatory.” 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
1.4.  During discussions, some members of the Committee raised doubts about the 
linking of Aadhaar with EPIC of non-citizens, which led the Committee to suggest 
that the ECI should establish a legal provision or an alternative mechanism to ensure 
that non-citizens with Aadhaar are not included in the voter list. Additionally, citizens 
who have not yet linked their Aadhaar should be assured that they can still exercise 
their legal right to vote. The Committee emphasized the importance of these 
clarifications in addressing concerns related to the implementation of a Common 
Electoral Roll (Para 1.49) 

9 
 
Action Taken 
1.5 Comments of this Department: In this regard, it may be stated that the said 
recommendation pertains to the ECI and they have submitted the comments as under:-  
1.6 Comments received from the ECI: “As per Section 16 of RP Act, 1950 a non-
citizen is disqualified for registration in an electoral roll. Therefore, a non-citizen is 
not allowed to enroll even if he possesses Aadhaar card. Aadhar is not a citizenship 
document. Further, under Section 31 of the RP Act, 1950 making false declaration in 
connection with the preparation, revision or correction of an electoral roll or the 
inclusion or exclusion of any entry in or from an electoral roll is a punishable offence 
with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine or both. 
Hence, there is already legal provision available in the present election law to prevent 
a non-citizen from enrolment. 
1.7 For registration as an elector in an Assembly or Parliamentary Constituency, 
person must not be less than 18 years (on the qualifying date prescribed by law) and 
citizen of India having ordinarily resident in the constituency concerned. 
1.8 Further, vide Commission's letter dated 04.07.2022; it has been made amply 
clear that submission of Aadhaar by electors is voluntary and their names cannot be 
struck off from the electoral database merely because of their inability to furnish 
Aadhaar.” 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
1.9  The Committee recommends that the Legislative Department and the Election 
Commission collaborate to examine the effects of the delimitation process, especially 
in challenging terrains. The Election Commission lacks the authority to direct State 
Election Commissions or appraise the performance of State Election Commissioners. 
The Committee draws the attention of ECI to the fact that treating all regions in India 
as identical can pose a significant risk. It is therefore imperative to recognize this 
reality and take appropriate measures to address it. (Para 1.55) 
Action Taken  
1.10 Comments received from the ECI: “The recommendations of the Committee 
have been noted for future reference.” 
1.11 Comments of this Department: The recommendations of the Committee have 
been noted for future reference. 
 

10 
 
Recommendation/Observation  
 
1.12 The Committee has taken note of the potential benefits that could be derived 
from the creation of a Common Electoral Roll through the collaborative participation 
of officials who serve in both the Election Commission of India and State Election 
Commissions. However, it stresses the importance of proper constitutional and 
statutory authorization before the Election Commission takes charge of creating or 
managing electoral rolls for State Election Commissions. The Committee suggests 
that States may continue to utilize the electoral roll of the Election Commission until 
necessary legal changes have been made. Furthermore, the Committee strongly 
recommends that the Election Commission of India and the Legislative Department 
collaborate to preserve the rights of both State Election Commissions and State 
Governments when preparing the Common Electoral Roll. (Para 1.56) 
Action Taken  
1.13 Comments received from the ECI: “In this connection, it is informed that ECI 
facilitates State Election Commissions by sharing its electoral roll data with them 
upon their request in the manner and form as requested, on which SECs carry out 
their amendments or marking of ward boundaries. 
1.14 So far, Election Commission of India has shared its Electoral roll data with 32 
State Election Commissions.” 
1.15 Comments of this Department: It is stated that the recommendations of the 
Committee have been noted by this Department. 
 
Recommendation/Observation  
 
1.16.  The Committee suggests that the Election Commission and Legislative 
Department collaborate to encourage States to utilize the Election Commission's 
electoral roll when creating their own until there is a change in constitutional and 
statutory provisions. The Committee strongly emphasizes the significance of 
preserving the rights of State Election Commissions and State while taking action. 
(Para 1.57) 
  

11 
 
Action Taken  
1.17 Comments received from the ECI: “The ECI facilitates State Election 
Commissions by sharing its electoral roll data with them upon their request in the 
manner and form as requested, on which SECs carry out their amendments of 
marking of ward boundaries. So far, Election Commission of India has shared its 
Electoral roll data with 32 State Election Commissions.” 
1.18 Comments of this Department: It is stated that the recommendations of the 
Committee have been noted by this Department. Further, it is stated that the reply to 
paragraph 4 may be again referred to.  
 
Recommendation/Observation  
 
1.19  The Committee observes that it is important to involve stakeholders in the 
process of creating fair regulations for defining reasonable declarations in election 
affidavits. This is crucial to protect innocent individuals and distinguish fraudulent 
declarations from unintentional mistakes. To ensure fair and effective elections, it is 
necessary to address the challenges faced by political parties and candidates. (Para 
2.30) 
Action Taken  
1.20 Comments received from the ECI: “Political parties may be asked to provide 
their views in the matter. Ministry of Law & Justice may please consider.” 
1.21 Comments of this Department: In this regard, it is stated that this Department 
has taken note of the recommendation of the Committee to address the challenges 
faced by the political parties and candidates during filing of the election affidavits. It 
is further stated that the recommendations of the Committee would be referred in 
future as and when electoral reforms are carried out on the issue. 
 
Recommendation/Observation  
 
1.22  The Committee strongly recommends that the RP Act of 1951 needs to have a 
clear definition of what constitute a false declaration/affidavit which is presently 
mentioned under Section 123(4) that covers corrupt practices, and concealment of 
information specified under Section 125A which specifies penalties for filing false 
affidavits respectively, so as to establish fair practices in election process. (Para 2.31) 
  

12 
 
Action Taken 
1.23 Comments received from the ECI: “Noted in the Commission. 
Further, the Commission vide letter no. 3/1/2011/5DR dated 3rd February, 2011 
(Annexure-B) (Reiterated in April, 2012) had already proposed an amendment to Sec 
125 A of 1951 Act, providing for punishment of 2 years imprisonment for filing of 
false affidavits by the candidates (Affidavit in Form 26) and to include this in sub-
section (1) of section 8 so that conviction will automatically lead to disqualification.” 
1.24 Comments of this Department: In this regard, it is stated that this Department 
has noted the recommendation of the Committee and whenever the proposals for 
electoral reforms are taken up by the Government the ECI’s proposal for amending 
the provision regarding false declaration shall also be considered. 
 
Recommendation/Observation  
 
1.25  The Committee also recommends that the penalties associated with these 
actions should be based on their severity of the act committed and be included as a 
separate provision in addition to or in place of the existing Section 125A that deals 
with penalties for false declarations. (Para 2.32) 
Action Taken 
1.26 Comments received from the ECI: “For providing different penalties, based on 
severity of the act committed, the information provided in the affidavit is required to 
be categorized. Ministry of Law & Justice may take a view.” 
1.27 Comments of this Department: In this regard, it is stated that this Department 
has taken note of the recommendation of the Committee. It is further stated that the 
recommendations of the Committee would be referred in future as and when electoral 
reforms are carried out on the above mentioned issue. 
 
Recommendation/Observation  
 
1.28  The Committee also recommends that if a candidate is found to have provided 
false Information, under the updated/new provision proposed by the Committee, they 
should be deemed ineligible for any benefits resulting from such election. This 
measure is aimed at ensuring a level playing field for all candidates and upholding 
the integrity of the election process. (Para 2.34) 
  

13

Recommendation/Observation

progress made since the Election Commission of India proposed the Common

concern about the potential impact on State powers, mentioned under Chapter IX and 

16 
 
IX A of the Constitution of India. The Committee therefore suggests that the ECI

2.10  The Committee observes that implementing a Common Electoral Roll, as 
proposed by the Central Government and ECI, is presently outside the scope of 
Article 325 of the Constitution. This article stipulates that separate electoral rolls 
must be used for elections to Parliament and the State Legislatures. To ensure that all 
actions are in line with the Constitution, the Committee suggests consensus shall be 
made in line with Article 325. The Committee advises the government to proceed 
with caution, adhere to the principles of federalism enshrined in the Constitution, and 
carefully assess the potential consequences before taking any actions. (Para 1.53) 
Action Taken

CHAPTER III 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS IN RESPECT OF 
WHICH THE COMMITTEE DOES NOT ACCEPT THE REASONS 
GIVEN BY THE MINISTRY AND REITERATES ITS 
RECOMMENDATION 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
3.1.  For elections to be truly free and fair, it is crucial to ensure that accurate 
information is provided to voters. The Supreme Court recognizes this importance and 
this Committee emphasizes the need to define what is considered a False 
Declaration/affidavit and when penalties, criminal action, or disqualification are 
warranted. It's important to note that minor factual errors should not be treated as 
significant enough to require penalization. (Para 2.28) 
Action Taken 
3.2 Comments received from the ECI: “Sec 125A of the Representation of the 
People Act, 1951 defines false declaration in connection with an election. Section 
125A provides that: 
"A candidate who himself or through his proposer, with intent to be elected in an 
election:- 
(1) fails to furnish information relating to sub-section (1) of section 33A; or 
(ii) gives false information which he knows or has reason to believe to be false; or 
(iii) conceals any information, in his nomination paper delivered under sub-section 
(1) of section 33 or in his affidavit which is required to be delivered under sub-
section (2) of section 33A, as the case may be, shall, notwithstanding anything 
contained in any other law for the time be in force, be punishable with imprisonment 
for a term which may extend to six months or with fine, or with both. 
3.3 It is for the Ministry of Law & Justice to define as to what constitute false 
information.” 
  

25 
 
Further recommendation/observation: 
3.4 The Committee notes that while the existing legal provision under Section 
125A does address the issue of false declarations, the lack of clarity and 
standardisation in interpreting “false information” continues to create 
ambiguity in enforcement. The ECI’s response, though legally valid, is 
procedurally insufficient, as it does not reflect a proactive approach in aiding 
legislative clarity or suggesting improvements in the operational framework.  
ECI, being the nodal authority on election administration, is best positioned to 
recommend technical and procedural refinements, offer a detailed proposal and 
assist the Ministry to frame clear provision, in this regard. 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
3.5  The Committee proposes that candidates who provide false information in their 
affidavits should be disqualified or declared ineligible, depending upon the severity 
of the action committed, regardless of whether they win the election.  The Committee 
believes this is essential to uphold the integrity of the democratic processes in 
accordance with the Constitutional mandate. The Committee recommends that the 
government sets up a verification process for affidavits and promptly informs the 
Election Commission of any false data to ensure adherence to regulations. (Para 2.29) 
Action Taken  
3.6 Comments received from the ECI: “It is for the government of India to take action.” 
3.7 Comments of this Department: In this regard, it is stated that the 
recommendation of the Committee at Paragraph 11 of chapter seven of the report 
mentioned above are general observations of the committee and thus, do not warrant 
a specific reply by this Department. Further in response to paragraph 12 of chapter 
seven it is stated that in view of the principle of separation of powers enshrined in the 
Constitution and to ensure free and fair election it would not be appropriate for the 
Government of India to be involved in verifying the Affidavits filed by the candidates 
fielded by the various political parties.  
Further recommendation/observation: 
3.8 The Committee's recommendation is a well-reasoned proposal to address 
a systemic gap to create a transparent and reliable affidavit verification 
mechanism. This would enhance electoral integrity and strengthen public trust 
in the democratic process.  However, both the ECI and the Department’s 
responses seems to be evasive and non-committal. The ECI shifts responsibility 

26 
 
to the government without offering any initiative or alternative mechanism. The 
Department, on the other hand, rejects the recommendation outright by 
invoking the principle of separation of powers, without exploring collaborative 
or independent institutional solutions.  This reflects a missed opportunity for 
reform, where instead of working together to design a verification framework 
involving independent agencies or third-party audits, both institutions have 
chosen to maintain the status quo. The Committee reaffirms that ensuring 
truthful disclosures in candidate affidavits is a shared institutional responsibility 
and requires a coordinated and accountable approach.  The Committee, 
therefore, recommends that the Government should use technology and data 
analytics for cross verification of affidavits with Govt. records in real-time. 
 
Recommendation/Observation  
 
3.9  The Committee observes that the current punishment, which is only six months 
under section 125A, is insufficient and should be increased. The severity of 
punishment should be based on the severity of the offence committed. The 
Committee suggests that if someone files a false affidavit, their offence level should 
be taken into account and may be added to the list of offences under section 8(1) that 
lead to disqualification. (Para 2.35) 
 
Action Taken 
 
3.10 Comments received from the ECI: “Comments against Para 2.31 of the report 
may please be referred to.” 
3.11 Comments of this Department: In this regard, it is stated that this Department 
has noted the recommendation of the Committee and the reform of amending the 
provision regarding false declaration is currently under examination of the 
government. 
Further recommendation/observation: 
3.12 The Committee strongly emphasizes that filing false affidavits undermines 
the sanctity of the electoral process and deceives voters, which should be treated 
as a grave electoral offence. Mere acknowledgement that the matter is under 
examination, without any definite timeline or indication of progress will not 
solve the problems.  The Committee, therefore, reiterates that punishment 
under Section 125A be enhanced to act as a deterrent, and that the nature and 
impact of the falsehood should guide the degree of punishment. The Committee 

27 
 
also urges that serious instances of deliberate misrepresentation in affidavits 
should be included as grounds for disqualification under Section 8(1) of the 
Representation of the People Act, 1951.  The Committee expects the Department 
to expedite the examination of this issue and furnish a detailed status report 
within a reasonable timeframe. 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
3.13  The Committee suggests that in order to ensure fair elections and to protect 
citizens' rights according to Article 19(1)(a), punishment under section 125A should 
be increased to a maximum of two years in prison and a fine. However, this penalty 
should only be applied in exceptional cases, and not for minor errors or unintentional 
mistakes. Under the new provision, submitting a false affidavit should be considered 
a violation of constitutional provisions, and an election may be invalidated under sub-
Section 1(d) (iv) of section 100 of the Act. (Para 2.36) 
Action Taken  
3.14 Comments received from the ECI: “The Commission has already sent a 
proposal in this regard to Government of India vide its letter dated 
03/02/2011(Annexure-B).” 
3.15 Comments of this Department: In this regard, it is stated that this Department 
has taken note of the recommendation of the Committee. It is further stated that the 
recommendations of the Committee would be referred in future as and when electoral 
reforms are carried out on the above mentioned issue. Moreover, it is stated that the 
Law Commission in its 244th Report on Electoral Disqualifications also considered 
the issue and the report of the Law Commission is under consideration of the 
government. 
Further recommendation/observation: 
3.16 The Committee notes with concern that despite earlier recommendations 
from the Election Commission of India and observations made in the Law 
Commission’s 244th Report, there has been no concrete progress or timeline 
provided by the Department.  The Committee, therefore recommends that the 
Department should submit a detailed status report on the present stage of 
examination of these proposals, including any inter-ministerial consultations 
held, drafts prepared, or timelines envisioned for legislative action. 
  

28 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
3.17  Further, the Committee proposes that intentionally disregarding other 
requirements, such as the furnishing of information outlined in section 33A of the RP 
Act, 1951, as listed in section 125A, should be considered a "Corrupt Practice" under 
section 123 of the RP Act, 1951, for the case of filing election petitions. (Para 2.37) 
Action Taken  
3.18 Comments received from the ECI:  “Noted in the Commission.” 
3.19 Comments of this Department: In this regard, it is stated that this Department 
has taken note of the recommendation of the Committee. Moreover, it is stated that 
the Law Commission in its 244th Report on Electoral Disqualifications also 
considered the issue and the report of the Law Commission is under consideration of

Further recommendation/observation:  
3.20 The Committee urges Government to act on the recommendation without 
awaiting consideration of the Law Commission’s report. Government should 
consult ECI and other relevant stakeholders to introduce appropriate 
amendments to Section 123 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, so

seriously impacts the integrity of electoral democracy. 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
3.21  The Committee also recommends empowering the Commission of India with 
the authority to review and make a verdict on the falsification of affidavits based on 
referral from the Returning Officer. The Committee also suggests expediting the 
resolution of disqualification cases, as prolonged litigation undermines the intended 
purpose of the legal provisions. (Para 2.39) 
  

29 
 
Action Taken 
3.22 Comments received from the ECI:  “This has been noted in the Commission.” 
3.23 Comments of this Department: It is stated that this recommendation of the 
Committee has been noted in the Department. Further, it is stated that the delay in 
court cases are beyond the purview of this Department and the Government cannot 
direct the courts to take action. 
Further recommendation/observation: 
3.24 The Committee’s recommendation addresses a major structural 
deficiency in enforcement of electoral laws and attempts to streamline resolution 
of such cases and reduce reliance on slow-moving judicial processes by 
emphasizing that ECI be given adjudicatory powers to decide on false affidavit 
cases referral by RO. However, the Committee observes that response of both 
ECI and Department is not committal. Merely “noting” the recommendation, 
without evaluating feasibility or proposing a legislative mechanism will not 
suffice to tackle electoral fraud. Also, while judicial delays may indeed lie 
outside executive control, government may legislate or propose special fast-track 
mechanisms or tribunals, to decide on candidate disqualification.  The 
Committee, therefore, reiterates its recommendations the given its 132nd report 
of the Committee and also suggests for expediting the matter through active 
institutional collaboration and prompt legislative follow up. 
Recommendation/Observation  
3.25  The Committee suggests reducing the minimum age requirement for Assembly 
Elections candidacy. The Committee believes that this measure can promote a wider 
range of viewpoints in policy deliberations and results. Additionally, younger 
candidates can help connect different generations, facilitating discussions and 
cooperation. This can boost the credibility and faith in the political process. (Para 
3.23)  
Action Taken  
3.26 Comments received from the ECI: “No suggestion and recommendation has 
been made in the Para 3.20, 3.21 and 3.22 of the report and action on the Para 3.23 of 
the report pertain to Government of India.” 
3.27 Comments of this Department: In this regard, it is stated that the 
recommendations of the Committee at Paragraphs 3.20, 3.21 and 3.22 of the report 
are general observations of the committee and hence, require no action and thus, do 

30 
 
not warrant a specific reply by this Department. It is further, stated with respect to 
recommendation at paragraph 3.23 of the Committee Report it is stated that this 
Department concurs with the view of Election Commission on the above mentioned 
issue which has been stated in the following in Paragraph 3.11 at page 47 of the 
report and reads as under:- 
3.28 “According to the Election Commission of India, unless compelling reasons 
exist to alter a provision of the Constitution, it should remain unchanged. The 
Commission believes that this principle falls under the age requirement for eligibility 
to join Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, Legislative Assemblies, and Legislative Councils. 
The Commission has already considered the issue of aligning the minimum age for 
voting and contesting elections to Parliament, State Legislature, and local bodies and 
has found that it is unrealistic to expect 18-year-olds to possess the necessary 
experience and maturity for these responsibilities. Therefore, the minimum age for 
voting and contesting elections is appropriate. The Commission does not favour 
reducing the age requirement for membership of Parliament and State Legislatures 
and still maintains this view.”  
 
[Emphasis Supplied]  
 
3.29 Hence, in view of the Department this recommendation of the Committee does 
not appear to be feasible. 
Further recommendation/observation: 
3.30 The Committee recommends that the Department reconsider the proposal 
in view of evolving democratic trends and international practices that 
increasingly encourage youth participation in governance. For this, a 
comprehensive consultation process should be initiated, involving youth 
organizations, constitutional experts, and civil society stakeholders. 
Additionally, the feasibility of a phased or limited reduction in the minimum 
age, such as lowering it to 21 years, may be explored through a structured 
impact study to assess potential implications and benefits.

R E P O R T 
 This Action Taken Report of the Committee deals with the action taken by the 
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions on the recommendations / 
observations of the Department -related Parliamentary Standing Committee on 
Personnel, Public Grievance s, Law and Justice in its One Hundred and Thirty First 
(131st) Report on  the subject "Review of Function ing of Recruitment Organisations 
of Government of India" , which was presented to the Rajya Sabha on 3rd August, 
2023 and laid on the Table of the Lok Sabha on the 3rd August, 2023. 
2. The Committee had made 3 7 recommendations/observations in its 1 31st 
Report. Replies of the Department thereto have been categorized and scrutinized 
under three chapters on the basis of satisfaction of the Committee. These replies have 
been categorized as follows: 
Chapter – I:  Recommendations/observations which have been accepted by the 
Department, i.e. in respect of paras 2.47, 2.48, 2.49, 2.60, 2.73 and 
2.101 of the Report. The Committee is pleased to note that the 
Department has accepted those recommendations. (Total-6) 
Chapter – II:  Recommendations/observations which the Committee does not desire 
to pursue in view of the replies given by the Department, i.e. in 
respect of paras 2.4, 2.11, 2.12, 2.14, 2.16, 2.19, 2.21, 2.28, 2.29, 
2.41, 2.46, 2.53, 2.61, 2.62, 2.63, 2.67, 2.75, 2.86, 2.91, 2.92, 2.96 
and 2.106  of the Report. The Committee is satisfied with the 
explanations advanced by the Department and does not wish to 
pursue those as of now. (Total-22) 
Chapter – III:  Recommendations/observations in respect of which Committee has 
not accepted the replies of the Department, i.e. with regard to paras 
2.7, 2.9 , 2.39, 2.52, 2.76, 2.77  and 2.104 of the Report. The 
Committee does not accept the reasons given by the Department  and 
reiterates the same.(Total-7) 
Chapter – IV: Recommendations/observations (1) in respect of which final replies 
of the Government have not been received. The Committee expresses 
its deep concern that it did not receive the replies from the 
Government in respect of Committee' s recommendation s vide Para 
No. 2.85 and 2.34. (Total-2) 

9 
 
3. The Committee desires that the Department should furnish pointed and detailed 
Action Taken Notes in respect of all the further Recommendations/Observations 
made by the Committee in Chapter – III of this report. 
4. The details of the ATR have been discussed in the respective Chapters in the 
succeeding pages. For reference purpose, para numbers of the original report (i.e. of 
131st Report) have been mentioned at the end of each recommendation/observation.

10 
 
CHAPTER I 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN 
ACCEPTED BY THE GOVERNMENT 
Recommendation/Observation 
1.0    SSC has been conducting online examinations for quite some time now. NRA 
thus may consult SSC for finalizing the modalities involved in the pro cess of 
conducting the exam. Thus, the Committee feels will give NRA a broad idea about 
the way in which competitive exams are conducted. (Para 2.47)  
Action Taken  
1.1 NRA has noted it for compliance and has fu rther stated that it is in touch 
with various States/ Organization including consultation with stakeholders. NRA 
has carried out regular interaction with various stakeholders including SSC. In  fact, 
Chairman, SSC is an esteemed Member of General Body of NRA. The experiences 
and expertise of SSC in holding recruitment examinations have been shared to 
enable NRA to finalize the modalities involved in the process of conducting the 
exams. 
Recommendation/Observation 
1.2    The Committee also recommends that NR A should consult Railway 
Recruitment Board as well regarding the recruitment proposal being prepared, so 
that NRA can finish the task within the given timeline and without any criticism. 
Also, it needs to work on the modalities of actual conduct of examina tion and 
publication of results cautiously and on immediate basis. As two years have already 
lapsed, NRA cannot take another two years to get fully functional. (Para 2.48) 
Action Taken  
1.3 National Recruitment Agency (NRA) has noted it for compliance and 
further stated that M/o Railways has two representatives in the General Body of 
NRA. Principle Executive Director -Staff and Executive Director of RRBs, who 
deal with all RRBs are members. Once the decision is taken, as explained in 
response to 2.46 above, NRA will take appropriate action. 
 

11 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
1.4    The Committee recommends that NRA should move very fast and start from 
the reverse direction since if it conducts examination for class 10, the number will 
be huge. Hence, the Committee a dvises NRA to start with graduate level 
examination so that the number of candidates with required eligibility is reduced. In 
case it starts with an exam which requires eligibility of class 10 th, all graduates will 
automatically become eligible and hence t he numbers would be large and 
unmanageable.  (Para 2.49) 
Action Taken  
1.5 National Recruitment Agency (NRA) has noted the recommendation of the 
Committee for compliance. 
Recommendation/Observation 
1.6 The philosophy of speed and accuracy required by bankers are changing 
from time to time.   Around ten years back, the workload and the nature of work 
perhaps did not need any speed or accuracy.   But today, speed and accuracy play a 
very important role owing to the hundreds of Central and State schemes bei ng 
executed by the bankers and the nature of pro -poor schemes launched by the 
Government. The Committee emphasises that because of the technology being used 
nowadays, whether it is e -banking or online banking, Public Sector Banks have to 
cater to large number of customers including the Jan -Dhan Yojana account holders 
and hence bankers have to be very fast with public dealing and also absolutely 
updated on the latest technology.   They should not face any kind of glitches and 
slow down in the process of service delivery. (Para 2.60) 
Action Taken  
1.7 Department of Financial Service has noted the same. 
Recommendation/Observation 
1.8 The Committee notes that not more than one lakh  students or examinees can 
appear at one go.   This number is very small.   IBPS needs to take steps to increase 
the number of students who can appear at one go for the examination.   It means 
IBPS will have to increase the number of the centres.   As on today , maximum 
number is one lakh or one lakh twenty thousand.   So, they need to work out on the 

12 
 
modalities on how to execute this computer based exam so that the number of 
candidates who appear in the exams can be increased at one go. (Para 2.73) 
Action Taken  
1.9 IBPS is exploring the possibility of increasing the number of centers/ venues 
in collaboration with service providers and other testing agencies, so that more 
candidates can appear per session, as suggested. 
1.10 The new centers  will be ensured to meet the strict safety and security 
standards and other infrastructure norms stipulated by Service Provider/IBPS. 
Recommendation/Observation 
1.11 The Committee suggests that they may explore the possibility of bringing an 
Act to govern recruitment under this scheme.   The Committee notes that after 
serving four years on the job, 75 per cent of the soldiers will be discharged from 
their services, and only 25 per cent would be inducted into the armed forces, as per 
the extant rules, the que stion that remains is about the rest. To prevent disaffection 
amongst these Agniveers, which  apparently comprises of youth of this country, 
Committee suggests that the remaining Agniveers may be given reservation/ 
preference in other Government jobs so tha t trained persons and the skills acquired 
by them during the service in Forces can be utilised to the maximum extent 
possible. Some jobs where it is practical to provide preference to them are Police 
Forces, Parliament Security Service and any other Combat Force. (Para 2.101) 
Action Taken  
1.12 Decision has been taken by Ministry of Home Affairs for providing 
following relaxation/benefits to Ex-Agniveers on their re-employment in the forces 
for recruitment to the post of Constable(GD) /Rifleman in the Central Armed Police 
Forces and Assam Rifles: 
i. 10% of vacancies shall be reserved for Ex-Agniveers in the recruitment 
to the post of Constable (General Duty)/ Rifleman. 
ii. The upper age limit shall relaxable upto five years for the candidates of 
the first batch of Ex-Agniveers. 
iii. The upper age limit shall be relaxable upto three years for the 
candidates of Ex-Agniveers. 
iv. Ex-Agniveers shall be exempted from Physical Efficiency Test(PET) 

13 
 
INDIAN ARMY 
 
1.13  (a) Empowering Agniveers. Empowerment of Agniveers t hrough 
educational upgradation and skill certification during his/ her service period has 
been ensured as follows:-  
 
 (i) Ministry of Education. 
  
(aa) National Institute for Open Schooling (NIOS) .  Based on 
the training and course syllabus, the Agniveer shall be upgraded 
from Secondary (10th) to Higher Secondary level (12th). 
 
(ab) Indira Gandhi National Open University (IGNOU) .    
Based on skill & experiential learning, each Agniveer  shall obtain

(ii) Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship . Skill

(NSQF) levels, the following shall be accrued :- 
 
(aa) ‘Kaushal Praman Patra’ or ‘Short Course Skill Certificate’ 
as per trade as approved by National Council of Vocational 
Education and Training (NCVET).  
 
(ab) ‘National Trade Certificate’ or ‘Long Course Skill 
Certificate’ (ITI Certificate) as per trade under Directorate General 
of Training (DGT).  
           
(b) Reservations. The following reservations in various jobs under different 
ministries of Central Govt have been notified:- 
           
(i) Ministry of Home Affairs .    10% horizontal reservation in 
CAPFs.  MHA has also written to States and UTs for reservation in 
respective Police Services.  
 
(ii) Ministry of Defence .   10% horizontal reservation in all levels 
posts has been notified.  
 

14 
 
(iii) Ministry of Finance .   Banks have been directed to extend the 
loans to ex -Agniveers under various govt schemes for encouraging 
entrepreneurship. 
 
(iv) Ministry of Micro Small and Medium Enterprises .   Higher 
subsidies, 5% reservation in courses and loans under preferential 
schemes have been extended to ex-Agniveers by MSMEs. 
 
(v) Ministry of Railways.   Notification issued for 10% reservation in 
RPF & all Level -1 posts as also 5% reservation in all Level - 2 to 7

(vi) Defence Industry . The defence industry confirmed due 
preference to Agniveers and incorporation of suitable provisions in their

INDIAN NAVY 
 
1.14 The Agnipath Scheme envisions that the ‘Agniveers’ would be provided with 
higher academic qualifications and skill certification based on their military training 
and experience. In order to facilitate enhancement of education qualification of 
‘Agniveers’, I ndian Navy has initiated an Outreach Programme. Under the 
programme, IN has signed MoUs with National Institute of Open Schooling (NIOS) 
for award of Class XII cer tificates (for MR sailors) and with Indira Gandhi National 
Open University (IGNOU) to facilitate award of Degree/Diploma (for SSR Sailors). 
Further, in order to facilitate smooth and productive absorption of ‘Agniveers’ in the 
civil industry, IN has been a ccorded status of ‘Dual Category i.e. Awarding Body 
(AB) &Assessment Agency (AA)’ from National Council of Vocational Education 
and Training (NCVET). This has enabled IN to ‘Adopt’ industry accepted 
qualifications from the various industry -promoted Sector Skill Councils to be given 
to ‘Agniveers’ on completion of their four years in the IN. These certifications are 
aimed at enabling them to become skilled manpower in the civil society towards 
nation building. The suggestions of the committee w.r.t. absorption of Agniveers into 
other Government jobs particularly Parliament Security Forces, Police Force and 
other combat forces is concurred. In addition, absorption of 75% Agniveers, not 
selected in Armed Forces, is also recommended for Group ‘C’ posts  of State and 
Central Government Organisations through appropriate age and qualification 
relaxations. 

15 
 
INDIAN AIR FORCE 
 
1.15 Details of declared reservation by GoI, to Agniveer after completion of four 
years are appended below: - 
Department Reservation

 5% reservation in Level 2 and above. 
 Age relaxation of 5 years for first batch of

Department of

above ESM quota. 
CAPFs & Assam 
Rifles 
 Will recruit Ex-Agniveer to the post of Constable 
(GD)/Riflemen. 
 10% reservation of vacancies. 
 3 Years relaxation in prescribed upper age limit. 
5 years relaxation only for first batch of 
Agniveer. 
 Exemption from Physical Efficiency Test (PET). 
 
INDIAN COAST GUARD 
 
1.16 ICG is working out procedure and shortly coming up with modus operandi to 
comply with the reservation for Agniveer recruits. 
 
DEFENCE PUBLIC SECTOR UNDERTAKINGS (DPSUs) 
 
1.17 The following has been implemented to ex Agniveers who complete their 
tenure under the Agnipath Scheme, for job preference in DPSUs: 
(a) Based on the educational requirement released in the advertisement for 
Agniveers, the posts identified for Agniveers in DPS Us are Driver (Transport),

(d) 10% horizontal reservation for ex Agniveers will be applicable. The 
reservation & relaxation for the Agniveers will be as per the DPE/DoPT 
directives/guidelines. 
ARMED FORCE HEADQUARTER (AFHQ CIVILIAN) 
1.18 The details of 10% of anticipated retirement vacancies for the year of 2026 & 
2027, in various Civilian Posts in Group (A, B, C & D) / service, is reserved for Ex -
Agniveer, are being complied and projected to MoD/D(JCM) Reservation cell

BORDER ROADS ORGANISATION  
1.19 10% of reservation for ex -Agniveers in all rank/posts of the Organisation in
